context: To decide which way to move in the two-pointer greedy strategy, start with the same height array ht = [3, 8, 5, 2, 7, 7, 3, 4] and put the pointers at opposite ends, [i, j] = [0, 7]. From this common starting point we can compare moving inward from the taller board with moving inward from the shorter board.
description: The left pointer i appears above board 0, whose height is ht[0] = 3. The right pointer j appears above board 7, whose height is ht[7] = 4. Both end boards are highlighted. A light blue rectangle from index 0 to index 7 shows the water reaching the top of the shorter left board at height 3. The label below reads “i is at the shorter board, j at the taller board” and gives the current capacity as cap = min(3, 4) × (7 - 0) = 21.

frames.explanation: The left board (3) is shorter than the right (4), so the water can rise only to 3. The boards are 7 units apart, giving a capacity of 21. This is the capacity at the start of the search. The maximum over the whole array is higher.
frames.title: Initial positions of the two container pointers

summary: The container between the two ends provides a starting point for comparing moves at the taller and shorter boards.
title: Initial positions of the two container pointers
